text: note|On a turbocharged engine the exhaust length below is information rather than a target. A turbine does not reflect a usable wave back down the primary, so the manifold is built short and equal-length instead — the 3,822 cc total volume is what decides how fast it spools.

note|The plenum and runners come to 2,317 cc, and a shorter runner is chosen here for that reason rather than for its pulse. Keep it in proportion though: on an ordinary front-mount installation the intercooler core and its two pipe runs are around three quarters of what the compressor has to pressurise, and this page cannot see any of it. Plenum multiple is a real lever on spool and a small one.

watch|Exhaust back pressure is set at about atmospheric, which no turbine produces. Manifold pressure typically runs at or above boost, and the gas is denser for it — the primary sizing here will read large until that is set.

Keep it in proportion though: on an ordinary front-mount installation the intercooler core and its two pipe runs are around three quarters of what the compressor has to pressurise, and this page cannot see any of it. Plenum multiple is a real lever on spool and a small one.

watch|Exhaust back pressure is set at about atmospheric, which no turbine produces. Manifold pressure typically runs at or above boost, and the gas is denser for it — the primary sizing here will read large until that is set.
